s1.syndrome_frame: Early pregnancy with uncertain location and rising beta-hCG, complicated by pelvic pain and potential implantation outside the uterine cavity
salient_findings: Pregnancy of unknown location at 6 weeks of amenorrhea
Gestational sac with irregular margins and yolk sac in the anterior isthmic portion of the uterus on transvaginal ultrasound
Rising beta-hCG levels
Worsening pelvic pain
Fetal pole with cardiac activity in a sac traversing the full width of the anterior myometrium on repeat transvaginal scan
key_facts: 36-year-old woman with two prior cesarean deliveries and two first-trimester miscarriages
Serum quantitative beta-hCG was 16,124 mIU/mL at presentation
Transabdominal ultrasound did not locate an intrauterine or extrauterine pregnancy
Copper intrauterine device had been removed 2 months before her last menstrual period
Used one cycle of clomiphene
No chronic illnesses, does not smoke or drink, and is not on medications
Blood pressure was 113/70 mmHg, pulse 98 beats/min, and temperature 37.5 °C on examination
Abdominal, cardiorespiratory, neurological, and pelvic examinations were unremarkable
Serial beta-hCG measurements rose by 33% over 48 hours
Repeat transvaginal scan revealed a fetal pole with cardiac activity
Postoperatively, became hypotensive without vaginal bleeding

shortlist.label: Cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of two prior cesarean deliveries and presents with a pregnancy of unknown location, with a gestational sac and yolk sac in the anterior isthmic portion of the uterus on transvaginal ultrasound

shortlist.label: Interstitial ectopic pregnancy
shortlist.why_kept: Transvaginal ultrasound shows a gestational sac traversing the full width of the anterior myometrium, extending exophytically toward the serosa, which is consistent with an interstitial ectopic pregnancy

shortlist.label: Intrauterine pregnancy with placenta accreta
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of two prior cesarean deliveries, which increases the risk of placenta accreta, and presents with a gestational sac and yolk sac in the anterior isthmic portion of the uterus on transvaginal ultrasound

shortlist.label: Heterotopic pregnancy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of infertility treatment with clomiphene, which increases the risk of heterotopic pregnancy, and presents with a pregnancy of unknown location

shortlist.label: Scar implantation syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of two prior cesarean deliveries and presents with a gestational sac and yolk sac in the anterior isthmic portion of the uterus on transvaginal ultrasound, which is consistent with scar implantation syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's history of two prior cesarean deliveries, combined with the ultrasound findings of a gestational sac with irregular margins and a yolk sac in the anterior isthmic portion of the uterus, and the fetal pole with cardiac activity in a sac traversing the full width of the anterior myometrium, are consistent with a cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy.

rejected.label: Interstitial ectopic pregnancy
rejected.why: While possible, the location of the sac in the anterior isthmic portion of the uterus and its extension toward the serosa is more suggestive of a cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy.

rejected.label: Intrauterine pregnancy with placenta accreta
rejected.why: The presence of a fetal pole with cardiac activity outside the uterine cavity and the absence of endometrial fluid or free pelvic fluid make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Heterotopic pregnancy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of an intrauterine pregnancy in addition to the ectopic pregnancy.

rejected.label: Scar implantation syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is not typically associated with a viable fetal pole and cardiac activity.
